objective: Investigate newly available laboratory result LAB-0225; assess scope, plausible explanations and human-reviewed next steps.

report.assessment: LAB-0225 is a newly available, hash-verified action-level result: 1.23 action-limit ratio for BATCH-075's relative_bioburden_signal (123% of the 1.0 action limit; 23% above it), the highest of 153 reviewed lab records in the scoped package. Its review status is 'action' in both the LIMS export and the local review sheet, and the scanned review document's OCR line matches, but that OCR layer is value-unverified, so original-document verification remains open. Scope: BATCH-075 (Famotidine Injection, USP, sterile solution for injection, LINE-A) is the only batch with records on the incident date; the process support area environmental sample EM-0075 is separately at alert level (0.71 against an alert limit of 0.7), so exposure of other material in that area cannot be excluded from this package. What the evidence supports: one action-level process draw and one alert-level process draw taken five minutes apart per the recorded sample times (1.23 vs 0.79; a 0.44 action-limit-ratio difference, ~56% relative), an alert-level environmental sample in the same recorded window, otherwise nominal process parameters, and one low-severity AREA-CORE differential-pressure-margin event whose direction the source does not define. Sorting by availability rather than recorded sample time would falsely suggest an escalating trend; the recorded sample order is the reverse. Four competing explanations remain open: a true process excursion (H-1), a laboratory or sampling artifact with a documented invalidation precedent (H-2), environmental ingress (H-3), and a preliminary/final recording convention (H-4). Maintenance records show only planned VESSEL-01 inspections, with WO-0001 and WO-0002 confirmed closed and none dated after late October. Human-reviewed next steps: SOP-driven review of LAB-0225 with a retest/confirmation decision, an explicit hold/continue assessment by QA, engineering review of the AREA-CORE event, additional area sampling, and verification of the scanned original. This is a partial investigation: the OCR and narrative-document layers remain value-unverified, some maintenance and document content was not transcribed within the shared retrieval budget, and the decisive discriminators (independent retest, sampling convention, room-control recipe) lie outside this evidence package and are requested for human review. No product disposition, release, CAPA, external notification or manufacturing change is proposed or executed here; the MEDIUM severity is an advisory proposal and final severity follows the configured routing policy.

report.cross_scope_synthesis: Shared patterns: (1) The same two BATCH-075 process results appear identically in lims_export.csv, microbiology_results.xlsx, lims_review_local.csv and the scanned review PDF (PRE-LAB-001 0.79 alert; LAB-0225 1.23 action / 123% of limit); all four carry the same provenance tag, so they corroborate the transcription but do not constitute independent measurements. (2) Three microbial signals sit within one 10-minute window on the sample clock: process 1.23 (10:40Z, action), process 0.79 (10:45Z, alert), environment 0.71 (10:50Z, alert) - the process signal exceeds its action limit while the area signal is only marginally above its alert limit. (3) Process context is largely nominal: batch start 06:40Z, routine operator check 07:55Z, temperature/pressure/hold margins in expected bands; the single non-normal event is the AREA-CORE differential_pressure_margin (0.9615, severity 'low') whose direction the source does not define. (4) Historical scope (SYN-0001..0074 units, 296 coverage units) shows only clock-metadata screening flags; package-wide distributions show just three lab results above 100% of limit in 153 records (one later invalidated) and four EM results at or above alert in the EM history - LAB-0225 is the highest value ever recorded in this package. Exceptions and limits: the two five-minute-apart process draws disagree by 0.44 action-limit ratio units, which keeps a laboratory/sampling artifact (H-2) as viable as a true excursion (H-1); no independent retest, organism identification, raw replicates, recipe/control definitions, calibration or chain-of-custody records exist in the scoped package; the scanned review page is unverified OCR with a garbled timestamp; and availability order (11:15Z then 12:00Z) must not be read as a rising trend because the recorded sample-collection order is the reverse (10:40Z then 10:45Z) - an ordering read from transcribed sample times, not clock-certified, since the package designates no resolved source clocks for these series. Maintenance scope: the only retrieved work orders are six planned VESSEL-01 inspections (Mar-Oct 2024, WO-0001/WO-0002 confirmed closed); no work order for PUMP-02, AREA-CORE or any sanitation/calibration item was retrieved, and the specialist sub-investigation's attempt to transcribe the remaining maintenance/quality/manifest narrative exhausted its shared retrieval allowance, so those documents were covered by targeted lead retrieval only, with unretrieved portions disclosed per unit.
